208.hindi_meaning: लॉजिस्टीक वृद्धि (सीमित संसाधनों के कारण वहन क्षमता के पास पहुँचकर स्थिर होने वाली वृद्धि)
208.example: The logistic growth model provides a realistic representation of animal populations.

208.english_meaning: The rate at which a population increases in size if there are no density-dependent forces regulating the population.
208.hindi_meaning: आंतरिक वृद्धि दर (प्राकृतिक रूप से वृद्धि की अंतर्निहित दर)
208.example: The intrinsic rate of natural increase is denoted by the letter 'r'.

208.english_meaning: The genetic contribution of an individual to the next generation's gene pool relative to other individuals.
208.hindi_meaning: डार्विनियन उपयुक्तता (प्रजनन के माध्यम से अगली पीढ़ी में जीन योगदान की क्षमता)
208.example: Organisms evolve to maximise their reproductive fitness, also known as Darwinian fitness.

208.english_meaning: A method or behavioral/physiological pattern adopted by organisms to maximize their reproductive success.
208.hindi_meaning: प्रजनन रणनीति (प्रजनन सफलता को अधिकतम करने का तरीका)
208.example: Different species adopt varying reproductive strategies depending on environmental pressures.

208.english_meaning: The product of reproduction of a new organism produced by one or more parents.
208.example: Some animals produce a large number of small-sized offspring.

208.english_meaning: Relating to the open ocean or sea, away from the coast or seabed.
208.example: Pelagic fishes swim in open waters and often produce numerous small eggs.

208.english_meaning: Non-living physical and chemical elements in the ecosystem, such as water, air, and soil.
208.hindi_meaning: अजैविक (पर्यावरण के निर्जीव घटक जैसे तापमान, जल, वायु)
208.example: Abiotic components like temperature and rainfall strongly influence life history traits.

208.english_meaning: Relating to or resulting from living organisms.
208.example: Competition and predation are important biotic factors in an ecosystem.

208.english_meaning: Not capable of being imagined or grasped mentally; unbelievable.
208.hindi_meaning: अकल्पनीय / जिसकी कल्पना भी न की जा सके
208.example: A natural habitat inhabited by just a single species is completely inconceivable.

208.english_meaning: Microscopic organisms, including bacteria, fungi, and viruses.
208.example: Soil microbes help break down organic matter and return inorganic nutrients.

208.english_meaning: Existing or occurring between different species.
208.hindi_meaning: अंतर-जातीय (विभिन्न जातियों के बीच होने वाला)
208.example: Interspecific interactions arise from the interaction of populations of two different species.

208.english_meaning: Tending to cause harm; damaging or injurious.
208.example: Parasitism is an example of an interaction that is detrimental to one species.

208.english_meaning: An interacting group of various species in a common location.
208.hindi_meaning: जैविक समुदाय (एक क्षेत्र में रहने वाले विभिन्न जीवों का समूह)
208.example: Plants, animals, and microbes interact to form a complex biological community.

209.english_meaning: An ecological interaction between two different species where both species benefit from the relationship.
209.hindi_meaning: सहजीविता (वह संबंध जिसमें दोनों जातियों को लाभ होता है)
209.example: Both the species benefit in mutualism and help each other survive in the ecosystem.

209.english_meaning: An interaction between organisms or species in which both are harmed due to limited shared resources.
209.example: Both species lose in competition when fighting for the same limited resources.

209.english_meaning: A relationship between two species where one benefits and the other is harmed.
209.hindi_meaning: परजीविता (एक को लाभ, दूसरे को हानि)
209.example: In parasitism, the parasite derives nourishment at the expense of the host.

209.english_meaning: The preying of one animal on others, where one species benefits by capturing and feeding on another.
209.example: Predation is nature’s way of transferring energy to higher trophic levels.

209.english_meaning: Tending to cause harm or damage.
209.example: This interaction is detrimental to the host and prey species.

209.english_meaning: An association between two organisms in which one benefits and the other derives neither benefit nor harm.
209.example: The interaction where one species is benefitted and the other is neither benefitted nor harmed is called commensalism.

209.english_meaning: An association between two organisms where one is harmed and the other is unaffected.
209.example: In amensalism, one species is harmed whereas the other remains unaffected.

209.english_meaning: Capable of making its own food from simple inorganic substances using light or chemical energy.
209.example: Green plants are autotrophic organisms that fix solar energy.

209.english_meaning: The hierarchical positions in an ecosystem occupied by organisms sharing the same function in the food chain.
209.example: Predators help in transferring energy to higher trophic levels.
Animals eating plants are categorised separately as herbivores.

209.english_meaning: Channels or pipes for conveying something; here used metaphorically for pathways of energy flow.
209.example: Besides acting as conduits for energy transfer, predators play other important roles.

209.english_meaning: Introduced from another country; not native to the place where it is found.
209.example: When certain exotic species are introduced into a geographical area, they can become invasive.

209.english_meaning: Tending to spread very quickly and undesirably or harmfully.
209.example: The exotic cactus became invasive and started spreading fast across the land.

209.english_meaning: Widespread destruction or great confusion and disorder.
209.example: The prickly pear cactus caused havoc by spreading rapidly into millions of hectares.

209.english_meaning: The control of a pest by the introduction of a natural enemy or predator.
209.hindi_meaning: जैविक नियंत्रण (प्राकृतिक शत्रुओं द्वारा कीट नियंत्रण)
209.example: Biological control methods are used in agricultural pest management.

210.english_meaning: An animal that naturally preys on others.
210.hindi_meaning: शिकारी जीव (जो अन्य जीवों का शिकार करता है)
210.example: The lion is a fierce predator in the grassland ecosystem.

210.english_meaning: Relating to the area that is above water at low tide and underwater at high tide.
210.hindi_meaning: ज्वारनदमुख / ज्वार-भाटा क्षेत्र (जो ज्वार के दौरान पानी में डूब जाता है और उतरने पर बाहर रहता है)
210.example: Many unique crabs and starfish live in the rocky intertidal zone.

210.english_meaning: Animals lacking a backbone or spinal column.
210.hindi_meaning: अकशेरुकी जीव (वे जीव जिनमें रीढ़ की हड्डी नहीं होती)
210.example: Insects, worms, and jellyfish are all invertebrates.

210.english_meaning: To use or harvest a resource too much, leading to depletion.
210.hindi_meaning: अत्यधिक दोहन करना (किसी संसाधन या जीव का अत्यधिक उपयोग करना)
210.example: If a species overexploits its food source, both populations may crash.

210.english_meaning: Acting with or showing care and thought for the future; cautious.
210.hindi_meaning: समझदार / विवेकपूर्ण (जो भविष्य को ध्यान में रखकर सावधानी से काम ले)
210.example: Nature's predators are often prudent to ensure their own survival.

210.english_meaning: Colored in a way that provides camouflage in the natural environment.
210.hindi_meaning: छद्म-रंगित (वातावरण में छिपने के लिए शरीर का रंग ऐसा होना जिससे पहचान न हो सके)
210.example: The chameleon is cryptically-coloured to blend with green leaves.

210.english_meaning: Hidden or disguised by blending in with the surroundings.
210.hindi_meaning: छद्मावरणयुक्त (रुप बदलकर परिवेश में घुल-मिल जाना)
210.example: The insect was so well camouflaged that the bird could not see it.

210.hindi_meaning: शाकाहारी / पादप-भक्षी (पौधों या उनके अंगों को खाने वाला)
210.example: Caterpillars are phytophagous insects that feed heavily on leaves.

210.english_meaning: Relating to the form or structure of living organisms.
210.hindi_meaning: कारकीय / आकारिकी (जीवों की बाहरी बनावट या संरचना से संबंधित)
210.example: Thorns and spines are morphological defences in plants.

210.english_meaning: To hinder, restrain, or prevent an action or process.
210.hindi_meaning: बाधा डालना / रोकना (किसी प्रक्रिया या विकास को मंद करना)
210.example: Certain plant chemicals can inhibit digestion in herbivores.

210.english_meaning: A class of organic compounds that increase the output force of the heart and increase its rate contractions, often toxic.
210.hindi_meaning: हृदय संबंधी ग्लाइकोसाइड (एक विषैला रसायन जो पौधों द्वारा सुरक्षा के लिए उत्पन्न किया जाता है)
210.example: Calotropis produces strong cardiac glycosides to deter grazing cattle.

210.english_meaning: Feeding on leaves, twigs, or other high-growing vegetation.
210.hindi_meaning: पत्तियां या टहनियां चरना (शाकाहारी जानवरों द्वारा पेड़ों के ऊपरी हिस्से खाना)
210.example: Goats are fond of browsing on shrubs and thorny bushes.

210.english_meaning: Existing or occurring between different species.
210.hindi_meaning: अंतर्जातीय (दो अलग-अलग जातियों के बीच होने वाला)
210.example: Interspecific competition occurs when two different species fight for the same limited resources.

210.english_meaning: Having great power, influence, or effect.
210.example: Competition is a potent driving force in organic evolution.

210.english_meaning: Plankton consisting of small animals and the immature stages of larger animals.
210.hindi_meaning: प्लवक प्राणी / जंतु प्लवक (पानी में तैरने वाले सूक्ष्म जीव)
210.example: Flamingos feed extensively on small zooplankton found in shallow lakes.

211.english_meaning: A type of competition where the feeding efficiency of one species is reduced due to the inhibiting presence of another, even when resources are abundant.
211.hindi_meaning: हस्तक्षेपी प्रतिस्पर्धा - एक प्रकार की प्रतिस्पर्धा जिसमें संसाधनों की प्रचुरता के बावजूद एक प्रजाति की भोजन ग्रहण करने की दक्षता दूसरी प्रजाति की उपस्थिति से कम हो जाती है।
211.example: Interference competition can occur between species even when food and space are abundant.

211.english_meaning: The ecological principle that two species competing for the same limiting resources cannot coexist indefinitely, leading to the elimination of the inferior species.
211.hindi_meaning: स्पर्धात्मक अपवर्जन - वह सिद्धांत जिसके अनुसार सीमित संसाधनों के लिए प्रतिस्पर्धा करने वाली दो प्रजातियाँ अनिश्चित काल तक एक साथ नहीं रह सकतीं।
211.example: Gause's competitive exclusion principle explains how superior species can eliminate inferior ones.

211.english_meaning: The expansion of a species' distributional range when a competing species is experimentally or naturally removed.
211.hindi_meaning: स्पर्धात्मक उन्मुक्ति - किसी प्रतियोगी प्रजाति के हटाए जाने पर दूसरी प्रजाति के भौगोलिक वितरण क्षेत्र का विस्तार होना।
211.example: The removal of the dominant competitor led to a clear competitive release for the smaller species.

211.english_meaning: An evolutionary adaptation where competing species divide a niche to avoid direct competition, such as by using different foraging times or patterns.
211.hindi_meaning: संसाधन विभाजन - प्रतिस्पर्धा से बचने के लिए प्रतिस्पर्धी प्रजातियों द्वारा भोजन या आवास के विभिन्न तरीकों को अपनाना।
211.example: Resource partitioning allows closely related warbler species to coexist on the same tree.

211.english_meaning: A symbiotic relationship where one organism benefits at the expense of another, usually living on or inside it.
211.hindi_meaning: परजीविता - एक ऐसा संबंध जिसमें एक जीव (परजीवी) दूसरे जीव को नुकसान पहुँचाकर लाभ प्राप्त करता है।
211.example: Parasitism is a common mode of life that ensures free lodging and meals for the organism.

211.english_meaning: Existing or occurring between different species.
211.hindi_meaning: अंतर-जातीय - विभिन्न प्रजातियों के बीच होने वाला।
211.example: Ecologists study interspecific competition to understand community dynamics.

211.english_meaning: The act of searching for wild food or provisions.
211.hindi_meaning: भोजन की तलाश - भोजन या संसाधनों की खोज करने की प्रक्रिया।
211.example: Different foraging patterns help the birds avoid competition for food.

211.english_meaning: Pointing to a conclusion without providing direct evidence.
211.hindi_meaning: परिस्थितिजन्य - जो प्रत्यक्ष प्रमाण के बजाय परिस्थितियों पर आधारित हो।
211.example: Strong circumstantial evidence exists for competitive exclusion in the Galapagos Islands.

211.hindi_meaning: आंतरिक या स्वाभाविक - जो किसी वस्तु या जीव का मूल गुण हो।
211.example: The intrinsic rate of increase measures the fitness of a species.

211.english_meaning: Relating to the area that is above water at low tide and underwater at high tide.
211.hindi_meaning: ज्वारनदमुखीय / अंतर-ज्वारीय क्षेत्र - समुद्र तट का वह क्षेत्र जो उच्च ज्वार में डूब जाता है और निम्न ज्वार में बाहर आ जाता है।
211.example: The larger barnacle dominates the rocky intertidal area of Scotland.

211.english_meaning: Serving to prove a case; decisive or convincing.
211.hindi_meaning: निर्णायक या अंतिम - जो किसी बात को पूरी तरह सिद्ध कर दे।
211.example: Evidence for competitive exclusion occurring in nature is not always conclusive.

211.english_meaning: To exist at the same time or in the same place.
211.hindi_meaning: सह-अस्तित्व होना - एक ही समय या स्थान पर एक साथ रहना।
211.example: Closely related species evolve mechanisms to co-exist rather than face exclusion.

211.english_meaning: Relating to the geographical distribution of organisms.
211.hindi_meaning: वितरणात्मक - जीवों के भौगोलिक वितरण से संबंधित।
211.example: The species expanded its distributional range after the competitor was removed.

211.english_meaning: To completely remove or get rid of something.
211.hindi_meaning: समाप्त करना या हटा देना - किसी को पूरी तरह से बाहर कर देना।
211.example: The competitively superior species will eventually eliminate the other species.

211.english_meaning: A general statement or concept obtained by inference from specific cases.
211.hindi_meaning: सामान्यीकरण - विशिष्ट मामलों से प्राप्त व्यापक निष्कर्ष या नियम।
211.example: Recent studies do not support such gross generalisations about competition.

212.english_meaning: Relating to the branch of science concerned with classification, especially of organisms.
212.example: Biologists study traits shared across many taxonomic groups.

212.english_meaning: Parasites that can infect or parasitize only a single species of host.
212.hindi_meaning: पोषी-विशिष्ट (जो केवल एक ही विशेष प्रकार के जीव पर निर्भर हो)
212.example: Many parasites have evolved to be host-specific to ensure their survival.

212.english_meaning: To evolve together reciprocally, as two species interacting closely with each other.
212.hindi_meaning: सह-विकास करना (दो प्रजातियों का एक साथ परस्पर रूप से विकसित होना)
212.example: Predators and prey often co-evolve over thousands of years.

212.english_meaning: To act against something in order to reduce its force or neutralize it.
212.example: The parasite evolved special mechanisms to counteract the host's immune defense.

212.english_meaning: Able to stick fast to a surface or object; sticky.
212.example: Parasites possess adhesive organs or suckers to cling on to the host.

212.english_meaning: An organism, typically a biting insect or tick, that transmits a disease or parasite from one animal or plant to another.
212.hindi_meaning: वाहक (रोग या परजीवी फैलाने वाला जीव)
212.example: The malarial parasite needs a vector like a mosquito to spread to other hosts.

212.english_meaning: The act or process of living as a parasite on or in another organism.
212.hindi_meaning: परजीविता (परजीवी के रूप में रहने की प्रक्रिया)
212.example: Complex life cycles facilitate the successful parasitisation of the primary host.

212.english_meaning: A parasitic flatworm of the class Trematoda, such as a liver fluke.
212.example: The human liver fluke is a well-known trematode parasite.

212.english_meaning: Susceptible to physical or emotional attack or harm.
212.example: Parasites might render the host more vulnerable to predation.

212.english_meaning: Parasites that live on the external surface of an organism.
212.hindi_meaning: बाह्य परजीवी (जीव के शरीर के बाहरी सतह पर रहने वाले)
212.example: Lice on humans and ticks on dogs are common examples of ectoparasites.

212.english_meaning: Of pests or parasites present in large numbers, typically so as to cause damage or disease.
212.hindi_meaning: परजीवियों या कीटों से ग्रसित या आक्रांत
212.example: Many marine fish are infested with ectoparasitic copepods.

212.english_meaning: Parasites that live inside the body of their host.
212.hindi_meaning: अंतः परजीवी (पोषी के शरीर के भीतर रहने वाले)
212.example: Endoparasites live at different sites inside the host body like the liver and kidneys.

212.english_meaning: Relating to the branch of biology that deals with the form and structure of organisms.
212.hindi_meaning: आकारिकीय (जीवों की शारीरिक बनावट से संबंधित)
212.example: The morphological and anatomical features of endoparasites are greatly simplified.

212.english_meaning: A reproductive behavior in certain birds where they lay eggs in the nests of other species.
212.hindi_meaning: ब्रूड परजीविता (दूसरों के घोंसले में अंडे देने की प्रवृत्ति)
212.example: Brood parasitism in birds is a fascinating example of parasitism.

212.english_meaning: To sit on eggs in order to hatch them by the warmth of the body.
212.example: The parasitic bird lets the host incubate its eggs.

213.english_meaning: A parasitic behavior in which certain species (like the cuckoo) lay their eggs in the nests of other birds.
213.hindi_meaning: परजीवी जनन (वह प्रक्रिया जिसमें एक पक्षी दूसरे पक्षी के घोंसले में अपने अंडे देता है)
213.example: The koel laying its eggs in a crow's nest is a classic example of brood parasitism.

213.english_meaning: An association between two organisms in which one benefits and the other derives neither benefit nor harm.
213.hindi_meaning: सहभोजिता (दो जीवों के बीच का ऐसा संबंध जिसमें एक को लाभ होता है और दूसरे को न तो लाभ होता है और न ही हानि)
213.example: Barnacles growing on the back of a whale is an example of commensalism.

213.english_meaning: A plant that grows on another plant, deriving its moisture and nutrients from the air and rain.
213.hindi_meaning: अधिपादप (वह पौधा जो सहारे के लिए दूसरे पौधे पर उगता है लेकिन उससे पोषण नहीं खींचता)
213.example: An orchid growing as an epiphyte on a mango branch does not harm the tree.

213.english_meaning: A small marine crustocrat with a hard shell that attaches itself to rocks, ships, or large marine animals.
213.hindi_meaning: बार्नेकल (एक प्रकार का छोटा समुद्री जीव जो चट्टानों या व्हेल की पीठ पर चिपका रहता है)
213.example: Barnacles attach themselves to the skin of whales to travel and filter food.

213.english_meaning: A small white heron commonly found feeding in fields near grazing cattle.
213.hindi_meaning: बगुला (वह पक्षी जो अक्सर चरने वाले मवेशियों के आसपास कीड़े खाने के लिए रहता है)
213.example: The cattle egret feeds on insects flushed out by grazing cattle.

213.english_meaning: To search widely for food or provisions.
213.example: Egrets forage close to grazing cattle to catch disturbed insects easily.

213.english_meaning: A predatory marine invertebrate with stinging tentacles resembling flowers.
213.hindi_meaning: समुद्री एनिमोन (एक समुद्री जीव जिसके शरीर पर विषैले स्पर्शक होते हैं)
213.example: The clown fish finds protection among the stinging tentacles of the sea anemone.

213.english_meaning: A long, slender, flexible arm-like appendage found in animals like squids, octopuses, and sea anemones.
213.hindi_meaning: स्पर्शक (समुद्री जीवों के शरीर के लंबे, पतले अंग जिनका उपयोग पकड़ने या रक्षा के लिए होता है)
213.example: Predators stay away from the stinging tentacles of the sea anemone.

213.english_meaning: Symbiosis that is beneficial to both the organisms involved.
213.hindi_meaning: सहजीविता (दो अलग-अलग जातियों के जीवों के बीच का ऐसा संबंध जिससे दोनों को लाभ होता है)
213.example: Mutualism ensures that both the interacting species derive benefits from each other.

213.english_meaning: Simple slow-growing plants that typically form a low crust-like, leaf-like, or branching growth on rocks, walls, and trees.
213.hindi_meaning: लाइकेन (कवक और शैवाल का सहजीवी संबंध)
213.example: Lichens represent an intimate mutualistic relationship between a fungus and algae.

213.english_meaning: A division of microorganisms that are related to the bacteria but are capable of photosynthesis.
213.hindi_meaning: नील-हरित शैवाल / साइनोबैक्टेरिया (प्रकाश संश्लेषण करने वाले सूक्ष्मजीव)
213.example: Cyanobacteria, along with fungi, can form lichens in harsh environments.

213.english_meaning: A fungus that grows in association with the roots of a plant in a symbiotic relationship.
213.hindi_meaning: कवकमूल / माइकोराइजा (कवक और उच्च पौधों की जड़ों के बीच का सहजीवी संबंध)
213.example: Mycorrhizae help plants absorb essential nutrients efficiently from the soil.

213.english_meaning: An organic compound that is a main source of energy for living things.
213.hindi_meaning: कार्बोहाइड्रेट (ऊर्जा प्रदान करने वाला कार्बनिक यौगिक)
213.example: The plant provides the fungi with energy-yielding carbohydrates.

213.english_meaning: To transfer pollen to a stigma, ovule, flower, or plant to allow fertilization.
213.example: Fig flowers are specifically pollinated by wasps in a mutual relationship.

213.english_meaning: Closely acquainted; very close, detailed, or thorough.
213.example: Lichens represent an intimate mutualistic relationship between a fungus and algae.

214.english_meaning: A symbiotic relationship between two different species where both organisms benefit.
214.hindi_meaning: सहजीविता / पारस्परिक सहकार (दो जीवों के बीच ऐसा संबंध जिससे दोनों को लाभ हो)
214.example: Mutualism between flowers and bees ensures both plant pollination and food for the bees.

214.english_meaning: Transferring pollen grains from the male part of a flower to the female part to enable fertilization.
214.example: Honeybees play a vital role in pollinating various crops and flowering plants.

214.english_meaning: Distributing or spreading seeds or organisms over a wide area.
214.example: Birds help in dispersing seeds across long distances after consuming fruits.

214.english_meaning: A sugary fluid produced by plants, encouraging pollinators such as bees and butterflies.
214.example: Butterflies fly from flower to flower to drink sweet nectar.

214.english_meaning: The process of two or more species evolving in close interaction with each other, adapting to changes together.
214.example: The close relationship between the orchid and its bee pollinator is a classic example of co-evolution.

214.english_meaning: A complete cluster of flowers arranged on a stem.
214.example: The wasp pollinates the fig inflorescence while searching for an egg-laying site.

214.english_meaning: The depositing or laying of eggs by insects or other animals.
214.example: The female wasp uses the developing fruit as an oviposition site.

214.english_meaning: The active immature form of an insect, especially one that differs greatly from the adult.
214.example: The wasp larvae feed on the developing seeds inside the fig fruit.

214.english_meaning: Puzzling, confusing, or astonishingly complex and varied.
214.example: Orchids display a bewildering diversity of floral shapes and colours.

214.english_meaning: The act of misleading or tricking someone by hiding the truth.
214.example: The Mediterranean orchid uses sexual deceit to trick male bees into pollinating it.

214.english_meaning: Strange or mysterious, especially in an unsettling way; remarkably similar.
214.example: The orchid petal bears an uncanny resemblance to a female bee.

214.english_meaning: To become aware of or interpret something through the senses.
214.example: The male bee perceives the flower as a potential mate.

214.english_meaning: Engaging in a behavior that mimics copulation with a non-living object or flower, often resulting in pollination.
214.hindi_meaning: छद्म-मैथुन करना (कृत्रिम रूप से संगतिकरण की नकल करना)
214.example: The male bee pseudocopulates with the deceptive orchid flower.

214.english_meaning: The state of looking like or being similar to someone or something else.
214.example: There is a striking resemblance between the insect and the flower marking.
Mutualistic systems must be safeguarded against cheaters that exploit the relationship.

215.english_meaning: Physical rather than biological; not derived from living organisms.
215.example: Temperature and sunlight are abiotic factors that influence plant growth.

215.english_meaning: Relating to or resulting from living organisms.
215.example: Predators and competitors are biotic components of an ecosystem.

215.english_meaning: Large naturally occurring communities of flora and fauna occupying a major habitat.
215.example: Deserts and tropical rainforests are examples of distinct biomes.

215.english_meaning: The action of coming to live permanently in a foreign habitat or area.
215.example: The population increased due to the immigration of birds from the north.

215.english_meaning: The act of leaving one's own habitat or area to settle in another.
215.example: Food scarcity led to the emigration of the herd to a new territory.

215.english_meaning: Becoming more and more rapid; increasing at an accelerating rate.
215.example: When resources are unlimited, the population growth is exponential.

215.english_meaning: Relating to a growth pattern that levels off as it reaches carrying capacity.
215.hindi_meaning: संभार-तंत्र (सीमित संसाधनों के कारण स्थिर होने वाली वृद्धि)
215.example: The logistic growth curve shows how populations stabilize over time.

215.english_meaning: The maximum population size of a species that an environment can sustain.
215.hindi_meaning: वहन क्षमता (पर्यावरण द्वारा पोषित अधिकतम संख्या)
215.example: The forest reached its carrying capacity, limiting further deer population growth.
The intrinsic rate of increase reflects the species' natural potential to reproduce.

215.english_meaning: The preying of one animal on others.
215.example: Predation is a key mechanism for controlling prey population numbers.

215.english_meaning: A relationship where one organism benefits at the expense of another.
215.hindi_meaning: परजीविता (एक जीव का दूसरे पर आश्रित होकर नुकसान पहुँचाना)
215.example: Ticks living on a dog are a classic example of parasitism.

215.english_meaning: An association between two organisms in which one benefits and the other is neither helped nor harmed.
215.hindi_meaning: सहभोजिता (एक को लाभ, दूसरे को न लाभ न हानि)
215.example: Commensalism is seen when small fish attach to sharks for protection.

215.english_meaning: An interaction where one species is harmed and the other is unaffected.
215.hindi_meaning: असहभोजिता (एक को हानि, दूसरे को कोई प्रभाव नहीं)
215.example: The trampling of grass by cattle is an example of amensalism.

215.english_meaning: A relationship between two species where both benefit.
215.example: Mutualism between bees and flowers ensures pollination and food supply.

215.english_meaning: Relating to the form or structure of living organisms.
215.example: Thorns are morphological defenses that protect plants from herbivores.

216.english_meaning: A group of individuals of the same species living in a specific area at the same time.
216.example: The textbook asks us to list the attributes that populations possess but not individuals.

216.english_meaning: In a way that becomes faster and faster over time.
216.hindi_meaning: घातीय रूप से / अत्यधिक तेजी से
216.example: If a population is growing exponentially, its size increases rapidly.

216.english_meaning: Belonging naturally; essential or inherent to something.
216.example: We need to calculate the intrinsic rate of increase for the growing population.

216.english_meaning: The eating of plants by animals or insects.
216.example: Plants have evolved various defence mechanisms against herbivory.

216.english_meaning: An action that occurs as two or more objects have an effect upon one another.
216.example: The interaction between the orchid and the mango tree is an example of commensalism.

216.english_meaning: Relating to ecology or the relation of living organisms to one another and to their surroundings.
216.example: What is the ecological principle behind biological control methods?

216.english_meaning: An interacting group of various species in a common location.
216.example: Students must be able to clearly define both population and community.

216.english_meaning: An association between two organisms in which one benefits and the other derives neither benefit nor harm.
216.example: Commensalism is an ecological interaction where one species benefits while the other is unaffected.

216.english_meaning: The relation between two different kinds of organisms in which one receives benefits at the expense of the other.
216.example: Parasitism is an interaction where one organism is benefited and the other is harmed.

216.english_meaning: The disguising of animals or objects to blend in with their surroundings.
216.example: Camouflage helps prey animals hide from predators in the wild.

216.english_meaning: Symbiosis that is beneficial to both organisms involved.
216.example: In mutualism, both participating organisms derive benefits from each other.

216.english_meaning: Existing or occurring between different species.
216.example: Interspecific competition occurs when two different species compete for the same resources.

216.english_meaning: Relating to population growth where growth rate decreases as population size approaches carrying capacity.
216.example: Describe the logistic population growth curve with a suitable diagram.

216.english_meaning: Qualities or features regarded as a characteristic or inherent part of someone or something.
216.example: Populations possess unique attributes such as birth rate and death rate that individuals lack.

216.english_meaning: Typical features or qualities of a person, place, or thing.
216.example: List any three important characteristics of a population and explain them.

217.english_meaning: A biological community of interacting organisms and their physical environment.
217.hindi_meaning: पारितंत्र (जीवों और उनके पर्यावरण का अंतःक्रियात्मक समुदाय)
217.example: A forest is a complex natural ecosystem.

217.english_meaning: Individual animal, plant, or single-celled life form.
217.example: All living organisms require energy to survive.

217.english_meaning: The surroundings or conditions in which a person, animal, or plant lives.
217.example: Plants adapt to their surrounding physical environment.

217.english_meaning: Scientists who study the relationships between organisms and their environments.
217.example: Ecologists study how human actions affect nature.

217.english_meaning: The regions of the surface, atmosphere, and hydrosphere of the earth occupied by living organisms.
217.example: The biosphere supports all life on Earth.

217.english_meaning: Made up of various parts or elements.
217.example: The global ecosystem is a composite of all local ecosystems.

217.english_meaning: Living on or relating to land rather than water or air.
217.hindi_meaning: स्थलीय / भूमि पर पाए जाने वाला
217.example: Forests and deserts are examples of terrestrial ecosystems.

217.english_meaning: Relating to water; living or taking place in water.
217.example: Fish and whales are aquatic creatures.

217.english_meaning: The tidal mouth of a large river, where the tide meets the stream.
217.example: Many unique species of fish live in the estuary.

217.english_meaning: The rate of generation of biomass in an ecosystem.
217.example: Solar energy drives the primary productivity of plants.

217.english_meaning: The state or process of rotting; decay.
217.example: Decomposition of dead organic matter enriches the soil.

217.english_meaning: A substance that provides nourishment essential for growth and the maintenance of life.
217.example: Plants absorb essential nutrients from the soil.

217.english_meaning: The process of breaking down or deteriorating.
217.example: Environmental degradation leads to loss of biodiversity.

217.english_meaning: The arrangement of and relations between the parts or elements of something complex.
217.example: We studied the trophic structure of the pond ecosystem.

217.english_meaning: Graphical representations showing the relationships between different organisms in an ecosystem.
217.example: Ecological pyramids show energy flow across trophic levels.

218.english_meaning: A biological community of interacting organisms and their physical environment.
218.hindi_meaning: पारितंत्र (जीवों और उनके पर्यावरण का अंतर्संबंध)
218.example: A pond is a self-sustainable ecosystem containing both biotic and abiotic components.

218.english_meaning: Non-living physical and chemical elements in the environment.
218.example: Temperature, water, and soil are important abiotic factors in an ecosystem.

218.english_meaning: Relating to or resulting from living organisms.
218.example: Plants and animals are the primary biotic components of the forest.

218.english_meaning: Vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels in an environment.
218.example: Forests show clear stratification with tall trees at the top and herbs at the bottom.

218.english_meaning: The state or process of rotting or decay, breaking down organic matter.
218.example: Decomposition of dead organic matter releases nutrients back into the soil.

218.english_meaning: The movement and exchange of organic and inorganic matter back into the production of living matter.
218.example: Nutrient cycling ensures that essential elements are continuously reused in the ecosystem.

218.english_meaning: Growing or living in or near water.
218.example: A pond is a simple aquatic ecosystem used to study ecological interactions.

218.english_meaning: Capable of making nutritional organic substances from simple inorganic substances using light or chemical energy.
218.example: Green plants and phytoplankton are autotrophic organisms.

218.english_meaning: Microscopic marine algae and plant-like organisms living in aquatic environments.
218.example: Phytoplankton acts as the main producer in a pond ecosystem.

218.english_meaning: Plankton consisting of small animals and the immature stages of larger animals.
218.example: Zooplankton serve as consumers feeding on phytoplankton in aquatic systems.

218.english_meaning: Organisms such as fungi and bacteria that absorb nutrients from non-living organic matter.
218.example: Fungi and bacteria act as key decomposers at the bottom of a pond.

218.english_meaning: The regions of the surface, atmosphere, and hydrosphere of the earth occupied by living organisms.
218.hindi_meaning: जीवमंडल (पृथ्वी का वह भाग जहाँ जीवन मौजूद है)
218.example: A pond ecosystem functions similarly to the biosphere as a whole.

218.english_meaning: The release of inorganic compounds from organic matter during decomposition.
218.hindi_meaning: खनिजीकरण (कार्बनिक पदार्थों से खनिजों का मुक्त होना)
218.example: Mineralisation releases nutrients back into the soil for reuse by plants.

218.english_meaning: Relating to the feeding stages or nutrition of organisms in a food chain.
218.example: Energy flows unidirectionally towards higher trophic levels in an ecosystem.

218.english_meaning: The unintentional or wasteful loss or scattering of energy or resources.
218.example: The dissipation of energy as heat is a natural part of ecological energy flow.

219.english_meaning: Total mass of living or organic matter organisms in a given area or ecosystem.
219.hindi_meaning: जीवभार या जैव संहति (किसी क्षेत्र में जीवों की कुल मात्रा)
219.example: The biomass of plants is measured in terms of weight or energy per unit area.

219.english_meaning: The rate of biomass production per unit area over a time period.
219.example: The rate of biomass production is called productivity.

219.english_meaning: The rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis in an ecosystem.
219.hindi_meaning: सकल प्राथमिक उत्पादकता (प्रकाश संश्लेषण के दौरान कुल कार्बनिक पदार्थ के उत्पादन की दर)
219.example: A considerable amount of GPP is utilised by plants in respiration.

219.english_meaning: Gross primary productivity minus respiration losses, representing available biomass for consumers.
219.hindi_meaning: शुद्ध प्राथमिक उत्पादकता (श्वसन हानि घटाने के बाद बची हुई उत्पादकता)
219.example: Net primary productivity is the available biomass for consumption by heterotrophs.

219.english_meaning: Organisms that cannot make their own food and consume other organisms for energy.
219.hindi_meaning: विषमपोषी या परपोषी (जो भोजन के लिए दूसरों पर निर्भर रहते हैं)
219.example: Herbivores and decomposers act as heterotrophs in an ecosystem.

219.english_meaning: Organisms such as fungi and bacteria that break down dead material.
219.hindi_meaning: अपघटक (मृत जीवों और पौधों को सड़ाने-गलाने वाले जीव)
219.example: Decomposers break down complex organic matter into inorganic substances.

219.english_meaning: The process by which complex organic matter is broken down into simpler inorganic substances.
219.hindi_meaning: अपघटन (जटिल कार्बनिक पदार्थों का सरल अकार्बनिक पदार्थों में टूटना)
219.example: The important steps in the process of decomposition are fragmentation and catabolism.

219.english_meaning: Dead plant remains and dead animal matter, including fecal matter, forming raw material for decomposition.
219.hindi_meaning: डेट्रिटस (मृत पौधे, पत्तियां और जीवों के अवशेष)
219.example: Dead plant remains and fecal matter constitute detritus.

219.english_meaning: The process where detritivores break down detritus into smaller particles.
219.hindi_meaning: खंडीकरण (डेट्रिटस के छोटे टुकड़ों में टूटने की प्रक्रिया)
219.example: Earthworms help in fragmentation by breaking down detritus into smaller particles.

219.english_meaning: The process by which water-soluble inorganic nutrients go down into the soil horizon and precipitate.
219.hindi_meaning: निक्षालन (पानी में घुलनशील पोषक तत्वों का मिट्टी में नीचे रिसकर जाना)
219.example: By the process of leaching, water-soluble nutrients go down into the soil.

219.english_meaning: The enzymatic degradation of detritus into simpler inorganic substances by bacteria and fungi.
219.hindi_meaning: अपचयन या केटाबोलिज्म (एंजाइम द्वारा जटिल पदार्थों का सरल रूपों में टूटना)
219.example: Bacterial and fungal enzymes degrade detritus through catabolism.

219.english_meaning: The process leading to the accumulation of a dark-colored amorphous substance called humus.
219.example: Humification leads to the formation of a dark-colored substance in the soil.

219.english_meaning: The release of inorganic nutrients from humus by the action of microbes.
219.hindi_meaning: खनिजीकरण (सूक्ष्मजीवों द्वारा ह्यूमस से अकार्बनिक पोषक तत्वों का मुक्त होना)
219.example: Humification and mineralisation occur during decomposition in the soil.

219.english_meaning: Animals that feed on dead organic material (detritus).
219.hindi_meaning: मृताहारी (मृत कार्बनिक पदार्थों को खाने वाले जीव जैसे केंचुआ)
219.example: Detritivores like earthworms break down detritus into smaller particles.

219.english_meaning: The regions of the surface, atmosphere, and hydrosphere of the earth occupied by living organisms.
219.hindi_meaning: जैमंडल (पृथ्वी का वह भाग जहाँ जीवन मौजूद है)
219.example: The annual net primary productivity of the whole biosphere is approximately 170 billion tons.

220.english_meaning: A dark-colored, organic substance formed by the decomposition of plant and animal matter in the soil.
220.hindi_meaning: ह्यूमस (मिट्टी में पाए जाने वाला काले रंग का कार्बनिक पदार्थ जो पौधों और जीवों के सड़ने-गलने से बनता है)
220.example: Humus acts as a vital reservoir of nutrients for plants in the soil.

220.english_meaning: Without a clearly defined shape, form, or crystalline structure.
220.hindi_meaning: अक्रिस्टलीय / बेढंगा (जिसका कोई निश्चित आकार या रूप न हो)
220.example: The substance formed an amorphous mass at the bottom of the container.

220.english_meaning: Relating to or caused by microscopic organisms like bacteria or fungi.
220.hindi_meaning: सूक्ष्मजीवकीय (सूक्ष्म जीवों या बैक्टीरिया से संबंधित)
220.example: Microbial action plays an essential role in breaking down organic waste.

220.english_meaning: The state or process of rotting, decaying, or breaking down into simpler parts.
220.hindi_meaning: अपघटन / सड़न (जटिल पदार्थों का सरल तत्वों में टूटना)
220.example: The decomposition of fallen leaves enriches the forest soil.

220.english_meaning: Relating to a system where microscopic particles are suspended evenly throughout another substance.
220.hindi_meaning: कोलॉइडी (निलंबित सूक्ष्म कणों से युक्त अवस्था)
220.example: Due to its colloidal nature, the material can hold a large amount of water and nutrients.

220.english_meaning: A large natural or artificial store or supply of something.
220.hindi_meaning: भंडार / जलाशय (किसी चीज़ का बड़ा संग्रह)
220.example: Forest soils serve as an important reservoir of carbon and essential nutrients.

220.english_meaning: The release of inorganic compounds from organic matter during decomposition.
220.hindi_meaning: खनिजीकरण (अपघटन के दौरान कार्बनिक पदार्थों से अकार्बनिक पोषक तत्वों का मुक्त होना)
220.example: Mineralisation ensures that inorganic nutrients are returned to the soil for plant uptake.

220.english_meaning: Dead organic material, such as plant leaves and animal remains.
220.hindi_meaning: मलबे / मृत कार्बनिक अवशेष (सड़े-गले पौधे और मृत जीवों के अवशेष)
220.example: Earthworms feed on the detritus lying on the forest floor.

220.english_meaning: A complex organic polymer deposited in the cell walls of many plants, making them rigid.
220.hindi_meaning: लिग्निन (पौधों की कोशिकाओं में पाया जाने वाला एक कठोर कार्बनिक पदार्थ)
220.example: Wood contains a high amount of lignin, making it resistant to rapid decay.

220.english_meaning: A tough, protective polysaccharide that forms the cell walls of fungi and the exoskeletons of insects.
220.hindi_meaning: चिटिन (कवकों की कोशिका भित्ति और कीटों के बाहरी आवरण में पाया जाने वाला कड़ा पदार्थ)
220.example: The hard exoskeleton of the beetle is composed mainly of chitin.

220.english_meaning: Relating to climate conditions such as temperature, humidity, and rainfall.
220.hindi_meaning: जलवायु संबंधी (मौसम या जलवायु से जुड़ा हुआ)
220.example: Climatic factors heavily influence the types of vegetation found in a region.

220.english_meaning: To control or maintain the rate or speed of a process.
220.example: Enzymes regulate the chemical reactions taking place inside living cells.

220.english_meaning: Life or metabolic activity in the absence of oxygen.
220.hindi_meaning: अवायवीय दशा / ऑक्सीजन की अनुपस्थिति में जीवन या प्रक्रिया
220.example: Waterlogged soils can lead to anaerobiosis, slowing down organic decay.

220.english_meaning: To hinder, restrain, or prevent an action or process.
220.example: Low temperatures inhibit the growth of bacteria and fungi.

220.english_meaning: Relating to the earth or living on land rather than in water.
220.hindi_meaning: स्थलीय / भूमि पर रहने या होने वाला
220.example: Forests and grasslands are examples of terrestrial ecosystems.

221.english_meaning: A biological community of interacting organisms and their physical environment.
221.hindi_meaning: पारितंत्र (जीवों और उनके पर्यावरण का अंतर्संबंधी समुदाय)
221.example: Energy flows through different organisms in an ecosystem.

221.english_meaning: Relating to the action of hot water, often deep under the ocean surface.
221.example: Deep sea hydro-thermal ecosystems do not rely on sunlight for energy.

221.english_meaning: In a way that relates to the process by which plants use sunlight to synthesize foods.
221.example: Photosynthetically active radiation is utilized by plants to make food.

221.english_meaning: Organisms that are able to form nutritional organic substances from simple inorganic substances.
221.hindi_meaning: स्वपोषी (अपना भोजन स्वयं बनाने वाले जीव)
221.example: Green plants and photosynthetic bacteria are primary autotrophs.

221.english_meaning: Moving or operating in a single direction.
221.hindi_meaning: एकदिशीय (एक ही दिशा में होने वाला)
221.example: There is a unidirectional flow of energy from the sun to producers and consumers.

221.english_meaning: The branch of physics concerned with heat and temperature and their relation to energy and work.
221.example: Energy flow in ecosystems follows the laws of thermodynamics.

221.english_meaning: To combine separate elements or substances to form a coherent whole.
221.example: Organisms need a constant supply of energy to synthesise required molecules.

221.english_meaning: Relating to the earth or living on land rather than in water.
221.example: In a terrestrial ecosystem, major producers are herbaceous and woody plants.

221.english_meaning: Having the characteristics of an herb; green and leaf-like rather than woody.
221.hindi_meaning: शाकीय (कोमल और हरे पौधों से संबंधित)
221.example: Herbaceous plants serve as important producers in terrestrial environments.
